title: Streaming pipeline: green the three world test files and commit
description: Close out TASK-26's working tree. Two failed attempts already wrote the whole pipeline and all the tests; what is left is bounded finishing: fix the two dangling references in the scripted-flight benchmark, diagnose and fix the one suspected test hang, get the full suite + typecheck + lint green, and commit everything. No new features in this task.

steps.details: app/src/client/world/streaming-benchmark.test.ts references MAX_SLICE_BUDGET_MS twice (in the console.log around line 132 and in expect(maxSliceMs).toBeLessThan(MAX_SLICE_BUDGET_MS) around line 144) but never defines it — the file fails before it can run. Define the constant: the per-slice contract is 8 ms of main-thread work (AC2); a measured slice = one in-flight unit (~1 ms) + at most the 4 ms between-unit budget. Measured on this box by the previous attempt: typical max slice ~3.5 ms, but GC jitter spiked it to 9.9 ms, and there was a rare 1-frame 3x3 miss before the heading-priority fix landed. Make the timing assert stable across repeated runs: the previous agent was adding slice percentiles — finish that (e.g. assert p99 of per-frame slice ms < MAX_SLICE_BUDGET_MS, log max + p99 + avg in the test output; a single GC outlier in the max must not fail the run). Keep the existing asserts: 3x3 near-neighborhood ready on EVERY flight frame (the no-pop-in contract, stronger than the 100 m edge margin), LRU peak <= 400, total tris < 400k every frame, max full-chunk work < 100 ms.

steps.description: Find and fix the test hang
steps.details: Running the three new world test files together previously hung (300 s timeout). The agent isolated chunks.test.ts (passes) and was isolating app/src/client/world/chunk-scene.test.ts when the iteration ended — the hang is not confirmed to be there. Run each file alone with a hard cap (npx vitest run src/client/world/<file> --testTimeout=60000) and find the offender. Prime suspect for a hang: unbounded wait loops — warmToNearBlock() in chunk-scene.test.ts, while (!streamer.isReady(chunkKey(2, 0))) streamer.update(...) in the LOD-swap test, and the pre-warm while (!restActive.every(...)) in the benchmark have no frame cap, so a build that never reaches done hangs vitest. Cap every wait loop (e.g. 4000 frames) with a clear failure message naming the stuck chunk, then fix the ROOT cause (a ChunkBuild/ImpostorBuild stuck before stage 'done', or a chunk never scheduled by ChunkStreamer.update).

From app/: npm run test (76 unit/integration files — whole suite green), npm run typecheck (tsc --noEmit clean), npm run lint. Run the full suite at most ~2 times: iterate on individual files first (each takes seconds), save the full run for the end of the iteration.

One conventional commit covering the whole working tree (pipeline modules are already in 342f5ad; uncommitted: the heading-priority fix in app/src/client/world/chunks.ts, the makeGeometry call fix in chunk-geometry.ts, the amplitudeM Pick<Planet> signature fix in src/shared/galaxy/surface.ts, the three new test files, and the frame-monitor.test.ts + debug-overlay.test.tsx extensions). Message like: test(TASK-26): streaming pipeline tests green — flight benchmark, scene, streamer (reference that the pipeline modules landed in 342f5ad). Leave the tree clean.

acceptanceCriteria: npx vitest run src/client/world/chunks.test.ts src/client/world/chunk-scene.test.ts src/client/world/streaming-benchmark.test.ts is fully green, and each file is also green when run alone
The flight benchmark is stable: two consecutive full runs both pass; its test output records slice max + p99, the triangle budget per frame, the LRU peak, and the 400-chunk memory estimate
All unbounded wait loops in the three test files carry a frame cap that fails fast with a named chunk instead of hanging
npm run test green, npm run typecheck clean, npm run lint clean
A commit exists (git log) and the working tree is clean
notes: STATE PICKED UP FROM THE FAILED ATTEMPTS (read .ralph/handoff/TASK-26.md for the agent's last messages):

- Committed in 342f5ad (wip TASK-26): app/src/shared/galaxy/surface.ts (extracted heightfieldChannels + generateChunkPlacement; VERIFIED bit-identical to TASK-5: surface.test.ts + snapshots.test.ts + shard.test.ts passed), app/src/client/world/chunk-geometry.ts (ChunkBuild resumable staged build: height -> placement -> near-positions -> near-index -> mid -> far -> done, one bounded unit per advanceUnit; ImpostorBuild = 1 unit; RING_TRIANGLES near 8192 / mid 2048 / far 2; near grid 65x65 shares border columns with the next chunk — no cracks), app/src/client/world/chunks.ts (chunkKey math, LOD rings 512/2048/8000 m, activeSet 13 at rest / 49 at speed >= 100, ChunkStreamer: 4 ms/frame budget, nearest-first queue, far-impostor window Chebyshev 6, drop-far-first under backlog with rate-limited perfWarn, LRU cap 400 that never evicts an active chunk, mountable(), reset()), app/src/client/world/chunk-scene.ts (three.js group, one mesh per mounted chunk, LOD swap = pre-built geometry pointer change, biome materials, per-ring triangle report + 400k gauge), app/src/client/perf/frameMonitor.ts (registerGauge/gaugeCheck/reportCategories extension), app/src/client/ui/debug-overlay.tsx (SURFACE line).

- UNCOMMITTED in the working tree (keep, do not revert): chunks.ts heading-aware priority (buildPriority: effective distance = dist - progress-along-heading; chunks ahead along the direction of travel build before equal-distance chunks behind — this is the fix for the no-pop-in AC at max flight speed; at rest it degrades to exactly nearest-first), chunk-geometry.ts 2-line makeGeometry fix, surface.ts 1-line amplitudeM signature fix, the three new test files, frame-monitor.test.ts (+ gauge/category tests), debug-overlay.test.tsx (+ SURFACE line tests).

- KNOWN ISSUES (the whole remaining scope): (1) streaming-benchmark.test.ts has two dangling MAX_SLICE_BUDGET_MS references — undefined identifier, file cannot run; (2) a combined run of the three world test files hung once (300 s); chunks.test.ts passes alone; the scene test was being isolated when time ran out; (3) GC jitter pushed one slice from 3.5 ms to 9.9 ms — do not assert on the raw max without a percentile or documented bound.

- DEAD ENDS / DO NOT RETRY: re-deriving the benchmark from scratch (it is 95% written and was measured green at 2.6 s wall before the dangling refs); changing the 320 m chunk size or the LOD ring radii (they are tuned: 13-chunk resting set = 9 near + 4 mid = 81,920 tris < 400k; 400 chunks x ~189 KB ~= 72 MB < 100 MB); removing the heading-priority fix to simplify (it is load-bearing for the pop-in AC).

- TEST FIXTURE: src/shared/galaxy/__fixtures__/surface-dev-seed-chunk00.json — seed + starId + planetIndex for planet 0 (Torolm, ice, landable); (160, 160) is the exact center of chunk (0,0). Tests drive the streamer with the REAL clock and the default 4 ms budget — warm-up is real frame-sliced work (~1 s), which is intended.

- CONVENTIONS: perf warnings go through setPerfLogSink from @client/perf/logger — every test that installs a sink MUST setPerfLogSink(null) in afterEach (already done in the drafted tests; keep it). FrameMonitor is instantiated per test — never touch the app-wide frameMonitor singleton from unit tests.

- BUDGET DISCIPLINE (45 min iteration): run individual test files first (seconds each), only then the full suite, at most twice; typecheck + lint once at the end. The suite has 76 files and has been green before, so a failure means one of the three world files regressed — isolate before re-running everything.
